### Handle Coplanar Points in Delaunay Triangulation

Source: https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/doc/source/tutorial/spatial.rst

Demonstrates how to identify points excluded from a triangulation due to degeneracy and how to use the 'QJ' qhull option to force inclusion by perturbing input data.

```python
from scipy.spatial import Delaunay
import numpy as np

points = np.array([[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1], [1, 1]])
tri = Delaunay(points, qhull_options="QJ Pp")
print(tri.simplices)
```

### Spatial Data Structures and Algorithms (scipy.spatial) > Delaunay triangulations > Coplanar points

Source: https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/doc/source/tutorial/spatial.rst

When computing triangulations, numerical precision issues or duplicated points can lead to degeneracies where not all input points appear as vertices in the final structure. These points are classified as coplanar and are recorded by the algorithm rather than being included in the triangulation. While these issues can arise from complex geometric configurations, users can utilize the 'QJ' option in Qhull to randomly perturb input data, which helps resolve degeneracies by forcing all points into the triangulation, though this may result in degenerate triangles with zero area.

### SciPy 0.12.0 Release Notes > New features > scipy.spatial improvements > Delaunay improvements

Source: https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/doc/source/release/0.12.0-notes.rst

It's now possible to pass in custom Qhull options in Delaunay triangulation. Coplanar points are now also recorded, if present. Incremental construction of Delaunay triangulations is now also possible.

### Qhull > Reference > The Quickhull Algorithm

Source: https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/subprojects/qhull_r/libqhull_r/Announce.txt

The Quickhull algorithm provides a practical approach to computing the convex hull of a set of points, which is defined as the smallest convex set containing those points. By combining the two-dimensional Quickhull method with the general dimension Beneath-Beyond Algorithm, it achieves performance improvements, particularly when input sets contain non-extreme points. This approach is conceptually similar to randomized, incremental algorithms used for convex hull and Delaunay triangulation, offering both speed and memory efficiency.

--------------------------------

### Qhull > Reference > Floating Point Robustness

Source: https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/subprojects/qhull_r/libqhull_r/Announce.txt

Computational geometry algorithms often struggle with the limitations of floating-point arithmetic, which can lead to significant errors if not managed correctly. Qhull addresses this by providing a robust solution for computing convex hulls in two, three, or four dimensions, where the output consists of 'thick' facets that encompass all possible exact convex hulls of the input. For higher dimensions of five or more, a variation of this method is employed to maintain accuracy and reliability.
